newsitem.title: FINLAND: HELSINKI CORRECTS LOWER, FINANCIAL SECTOR IN FOCUS.
newsitem.headline: HELSINKI CORRECTS LOWER, FINANCIAL SECTOR IN FOCUS.

text.p: Shares were mixed with strength
in the financial sector and forestries but the HEX was dragged
by weakness in Nokia and profit-taking in Huhtamaki which surged
18 percent of Friday, brokers said.
Skandia swapped over a million liquid Pohjola B shares for a
million vote-strong but illiquid Pohjola A shares and said it
was interested in more similar trades if the premium were not
too high.
This boosted hopes Skandia would prompt further
restructuring in the Nordic financial sector and lifted shares
in Pohjola and Merita, brokers said.
Pohjola B closed off its 105.00 markka year-high at 101.00
markka, still up 2.00 and Pohjola A closed unchanged at 104.00,
also after setting a year high at 106.00 markka.
Huhtamaki closed at 215, down 3.00, but traded at a 210.00
markka as investors took profits from its sharp gains on Friday
when it announced swapping its U.S. confectionery unit for one
in Europe and getting 1.5 billion markka in cash in between.
"(Huhtamaki) is now valued at net sales which is what
Leiras' value was (in the deal) so I think the downside is
bigger than the upside," said one. "If you bought at 170, it's
no wonder you want to sell at least some now," said another
Investors want Huhtamaki to announce good acquisitions for the money it has until they start buying again, brokers said.
Brokers still saw interest among investors to support an extended bull-run but this week was expected to bring little news and trade was seen relatively quiet.
On Tuesday, forestry group Enso's January-August result would gather some interest but it was not expected to change views that the sector is not recovering very quickly.
After the Helsinki close, Skandia said it had no plans to increase its Pohjola ownership further.
